topic_text: The value of goods and services produced in the UK.
text:
UK gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated to have increased by 0.1% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2023. Services output rose by 0.1% in Quarter 1 2023, with rises in information and communication and administrative and support service activities being partially offset by falls in education, health and public administration and defense. There was anecdotal evidence to suggest industrial action had an impact across a wide range of industries although we are not able to isolate the impact of these strikes from other factors across the wider economy.

Early estimates show that businesses were de-stocking their levels of inventories in the first quarter of the year, while there was a decrease in the volume of net trade and a small increase in private consumption in Quarter 1 2023.

topic_text: How much the production and services industries contribute to economic output.
text:
Monthly production output is estimated to have fallen by 0.3% in April 2023; this follows an increase of 0.7% in March 2023.

The monthly decrease in output in April 2023 resulted from a decline in three of the four production sectors, with manufacturing the main contributor to the monthly fall (0.3%), with smaller contributions from mining and quarrying (1.9%), and water supply and sewerage (0.1%); this was partially offset by electricity and gas, which rose by 0.6%.

Looking at the longer-term profile, production output for the three months to April 2023 rose 0.2% compared with the three months to January 2023; growth came primarily from manufacturing (0.7%), partially offset by a fall in mining and quarrying (3.4%).

The Index of Services (IoS) saw monthly rises in 10 of the 14 sectors: the main contributing sectors to the monthly rise in April 2023 were information and communication (1.3%), which contributed 0.12 percentage points to the IoS, and wholesale and retail trade; repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles (1.0%), which contributed 0.10 percentage points to the IoS; this was partially offset by falls in human health and social work activities (negative 0.9%), which contributed negative 0.08 percentage points to the IoS growth in April 2023, this sector was affected by industrial action (junior doctors), however it is not possible to quantify to what extent.

topic_text: Measures of demand in the economy for output that is produced.
text:
Retail sales volumes are estimated to have fallen by 0.9% in March 2023, following a rise of 1.1% in February 2023 (revised from a rise of 1.2%).

Looking at the broader picture, sales volumes rose by 0.6% in the three months to March 2023 when compared with the previous three months; the first three-month on three-month rise since August 2021.

UK business investment rose by 0.7% in Quarter 1 (Jan to Mar) 2023 and is 3.2% above where it was the same quarter a year ago.

The level of business investment in Quarter 1 2023 remains below that of Quarter 4 (Oct to Dec) 2019, the quarter before the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, by 1.4%.

Information and communication technology (ICT) equipment and other machinery and equipment, and to a lesser extent intellectual property products (IPP), contributed positively to the growth in business investment; this was partially offset by negative contributions from other buildings and structures, and transport equipment.

topic_text: Demand and supply of labour in the economy and how much employees earn.
text: The employment rate was estimated at 76.0% for February to April 2023, 0.3 percentage points up on the year and 0.2 percentage points up on the quarter.
The unemployment rate was estimated at 3.8% for February to April 2023, unchanged up on the year but 0.1 percentage points up on the quarter.

Average weekly earnings for employees in Great Britain in nominal terms (not adjusted for inflation) increased by 6.5% for total pay (including bonuses) and 7.2% for regular pay (excluding bonuses) in February to April 2023.

topic_text: Changes in prices of goods and services bought by consumers, as well as those bought and sold by producers in the UK.
text:
The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH) 12-month inflation rate was 7.8% in April 2023, down from 8.9% in March 2023.

Consumer price inflation can be influenced by the strength of domestic supply and demand, and changes in the UK prices of imports. The inflation rate also depends on price levels in the preceding year.

Producer output (factory gate) prices rose by 5.4% in the year to April 2023, down from 8.5% in the year to March 2023.

Changes in the output Producer Price Index inflation rate can be influenced by changes in labour and energy costs.

Producer input prices rose by 3.9% in the year to April 2023, down from 7.3% in the year to March 2023.

Input prices are influenced by raw material prices and exchange rate movements so are more changeable over time.

topic_text: UK exports and imports of goods and services and measures of foreign direct investment.
text:
The value of goods imports decreased by £0.7 billion (1.4%) in April 2023; after removing the effect of inflation, imports of goods fell by 0.4%.

The value of goods exports increased by £1.0 billion (3.4%) in April 2023; after removing the effect of inflation, exports of goods rose by a similar amount.

Both imports and exports of goods displayed an increase in trade with non-EU countries, while trade with EU countries fell in April 2023.

Despite a reduction in the gap in April 2023, imports from EU countries have been consistently greater than from non-EU countries since late 2022.

The total trade in goods and services deficit narrowed by £12.6 billion to £12.3 billion in the three months to April 2023 compared with the three months to January 2023, driven by a larger fall in imports than exports.

The trade in goods deficit narrowed by £10.7 billion to £52.5 billion in the three months to April 2023, while the trade in services surplus widened by £1.9 billion to £40.3 billion.

measure: FDI - liabilities (overseas investment into the UK)
text: UK direct investment liabilities were £1,287.6 billion in April to June 2016, up slightly from £1,272.4 billion in the previous quarter. FDI liabilities were following a broadly upward trend in previous years, before falling in January to March 2016.

UK direct investment assets were £1,414.7 billion in April to June 2016, up from £1,349.5 billion in the previous quarter. The value of FDI liabilities has fluctuated over the past two years, although remains broadly similar to levels seen in 2012.
